items.quote: And the LORD said unto Moses, Depart, and go up hence, thou and the people which thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land which I sware unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, Unto thy seed will I give it:
items.claim: In the text (Exodus 33:1), the LORD tells Moses to lead the people he brought out of Egypt away from where they are, toward the land promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob's descendants. This is what the text says, not a proven historical event.
items.object: Moses and the people brought up out of Egypt
items.place: from Egypt toward the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
items.mechanism: divine command tied to the oath made to the patriarchs

items.quote: And I will send an angel before thee;
items.claim: In the text (Exodus 33:2), the LORD promises to send an angel ahead of the people.
items.place: before the people on the way to the promised land

items.quote: and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
items.claim: In the text (Exodus 33:2), the LORD promises to drive six named peoples out of the land. The text describes this as a future promise, not something that has already happened.
items.object: Canaanite, Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite peoples

items.quote: Unto a land flowing with milk and honey:
items.claim: The text (Exodus 33:3) calls the destination a land flowing with milk and honey, meaning a rich and fertile land.

items.quote: for I will not go up in the midst of thee; for thou art a stiffnecked people: lest I consume thee in the way.
items.claim: In the text (Exodus 33:3), the LORD says he will not travel among the people. The reason given is that they are stubborn, and he might destroy them along the way.
items.place: on the way to the promised land
items.mechanism: the people's stubbornness creates a risk that the LORD will destroy them, so he withdraws his presence
